why our lady of knock is celebrated on two different days in ireland‘the anniversary of the apparition at knock is on august 21, but most of ireland honours our lady on august 17 in the liturgy.our lady appeared in knock on the night of august 21, 1879. though she never said a word, her appearance comforted many and gave a renewed vigour to the faith of the people of ireland, and encouraged many to turn to the virgin mary.the anniversary of this apparition is remembered each year at the knock shrine on august 21 with a special liturgy offered at the site of mary's appearance.however, the rest of ireland celebrates our lady of knock on august 17. it is classiﬁed as a "memorial," and parishes around ireland may celebrate our lady's apparition on that day.currently this celebration is only on select calendars, primarily in ireland, and not on the universal roman calendar.knock shrine social media explains that, "although the anniversary of the apparition takes place on the 21st august, the 17th august was chosen as the feast day of our lady of knock, as the 21st august is already assigned to st. pius x, the pope of the eucharist.”for the rest of ireland (and most of the roman catholic world), august 21 remains dedicated to st. pius x. the rationale behind the switching of liturgical days is to give more focus to a particular feast day, instead of supplanting one that is already being widely celebrated.’ (by philip kosloski)our lady of knock, pray for us! moves we keep in our prayers this week fr patsy mulholland who is moving from our neighbouring parish of loughguile to antrim as part of the annual clergy appointments. we also welcome canon colm mcbride who comes to loughguile. may god bless them and all the priests taking up new appointments in our diocese this week.parish of ballymoney& derrykeighancauseway family of parishes16th august 2026 twentieth sunday of ordinary timegreat faith, no boundaries today's gospel ﬁnds jesus seemingly reluctant to help a canaanite woman pleading for her daughter, telling her it wouldn't be right to give "the children's bread" to "the dogs." it's very strange - until we see what the lord is really doing. he's teaching his apostles, who had brushed the woman aside as a foreign outsider. through their back-and-forth, jesus reveals her deep faith and heals her daughter, showing the twelve that god's love has no borders of race or nation.it's a lesson for us too. as isaiah foretold, god's house is "a house of prayer for all peoples." we're called to carry that welcome beyond our church doors — meeting everyone with respect, and speaking up against the prejudice and division still so present in our world.

4.30pm. to keep in touch with our offers and to see pictures of our stock don’t forget our facebook page @oldandnewatno5parish of ballymoney& derrykeighancauseway family of parishes2nd august 2026 nineteenth sunday of ordinary timekeep your eyes on jesus in this week's gospel, jesus walks across the sea of galilee to his frightened apostles during a storm. peter, full of faith, steps out of the boat to walk towards him — but when he takes his eyes off jesus and looks instead at the wind and waves, he begins to sink. jesus reaches out and saves him, gently asking, "why did you doubt?”life brings storms of its own — worry, illness, family strain, ﬁnancial pressure — that can leave us feeling like we're sinking. this gospel reminds us that jesus is always with us in the midst of them, inviting us to keep our eyes ﬁxed on him rather than on our fears. as st peter later wrote, "cast all your anxieties on him, for he cares about you.” may the lord help us grow in faith and protect us whenever we feel we’re underwater.
